full_text:
The NFL is in “Phase Three” of the offseason, the final stage before contact practices begin with training camp in late July. We’ve seen a steady stream of news since OTAs (organized team activities) started in mid-May, and it always gets a little more interesting in June when veteran players are required to report for one mandatory minicamp unless they have an excused absence.

I went team by team to round up the most important fantasy headlines coming out of all 32 workouts. I’ll update this article through June 18, the final day of team activities in Phase Three. Check back often for regular updates!

\>Each news item will have a date at the end of it for when it was updated or added to the article…ADP data used in this article is based on the last month of drafts with our partners over at [Underdog Fantasy](https://www.fantasypoints.com/underdog#/)…Subscribe to our [Fantasy Bundle Package](https://www.fantasypoints.com/plans#/) to take your NFL research to the next level!

{{CTA|Underdog|omit=\[none\]}}

May 28
------

##### __Los Angeles Chargers__

+   *The Athletic*’s Daniel Popper [sees](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7313934/2026/05/27/justin-herbert-chargers-otas-takeaways/) __Charlie Kolar__ as the team’s #1 TE because of his “complete skill set”, ahead of __Oronde Gadsden__ and __David Njoku__. Kolar started his career fighting for snaps in a crowded TE room for __John Harbaugh__ in Baltimore, and he’s continuing his career in a stacked room for __Jim Harbaugh__ in Los Angeles. The Chargers handed Kolar $17 million guaranteed at the start of free agency, compared to the meager $850K guaranteed that Njoku received a couple of weeks after the draft. Kolar is unlikely to be a fantasy option playing next to the much more dynamic Gadsden and ahead of Njoku. Kolar’s presence is going to turn Gadsden into a frustrating TE2 if he moves into an __Isaiah Likely__ type of role. *(Added May 28)*

##### __Chicago Bears__

+   __Ben Johnson__ [told the media](https://x.com/BradBiggs/status/2060040773639324020) that he’s buying __Luther Burden__ stock heading into Year 2, adding that he’s been “extremely coachable.” Johnson is the one deciding on personnel and calling plays for the Bears, and he’s been driving the hype train this offseason. He previously said in mid-April that they need to get the ball in Burden’s hands as often as possible. Burden finished third in YPRR (2.83) and 11th in TPRR (26%) as a rookie, but he finished behind __Olamide Zaccheaus__ in route share at 41%. That’s about to dramatically change after the Bears traded __DJ Moore__ to Buffalo and Zaccheaus left in free agency. Chicago didn’t bring in any significant target competition outside of __Kalif Raymond__. It isn’t cheap to get Burden at his fourth-round ADP (43, WR21), but he has massive untapped potential heading into 2026. *(Added May 28)*

##### __Green Bay Packers__

+   __Josh Jacobs__ was arrested in Wisconsin on domestic abuse charges in connection with a disturbance on May 23. He was booked into Brown County Jail on five charges for the domestic violence incident, including felony strangulation and four misdemeanors. The NFL said that it is aware of the report and is in contact with the Packers, and Jacobs “vehemently” denied the allegations through his lawyers. The Brown County District Attorney’s Office released Jacobs from custody on May 27. No charges were filed at the time, but the investigation remains open, and a final charging decision will be made at a later date. Jacobs is coming off an RB10 finish (15.9 FPG) in his seventh season, and he was set up for a massive role once again entering his age-28 season, with just __Chris Brooks__, __MarShawn Lloyd__, and __Pierre Strong__ behind him on the depth chart. The investigation and legal process are likely to drag through the 2026 season unless charges are dropped or pled down. However, the NFL could place him on the commissioner’s exempt list during the investigation, especially because the charges involve domestic violence. I’m leaning toward Jacobs not facing a suspension this season in the initial stages of the investigation, but that could dramatically change in the upcoming weeks if incriminating photos or details emerge. I’m staying away from Jacobs at his current ADP (25, RB13) at the second/third-round turn. He’ll have to fall into the fourth round for me to consider selecting him as my #2 RB as things stand right now. Brooks is worth a late-round stab in case Jacobs’ situation gets worse, and Arizona RBs __James Conner__ or __Trey Benson__ could eventually be in play for the Packers if Jacobs is in danger of missing time. Stay tuned for this developing story. *(Updated May 28)*

##### __New York Jets__

+   __Kenyon Sadiq__ recently underwent a minor hernia procedure, but __Aaron Glenn__ [said](https://x.com/RichCimini/status/2060019452289102165?s=20) he’ll be ready to go for training camp. Glenn added that the Jets were aware that Sadiq would need the procedure when they selected him 16th overall. Brett Whitefield [described](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/te#/) Sadiq as a mutant — he posted a perfect [SPORQ score](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/stats/sporq/te#/) at the combine — who has the necessary receiving chops to be one of the NFL’s top TEs. The Jets didn’t draft Sadiq in the middle of the first round to waste him on the bench as a rookie, and it doesn’t sound like he should miss valuable practice time in training camp. He should get every opportunity to be a target-earner, and he can turn any pass into a long gain with his 4.39 speed. The last four tight ends selected in the top half of the first round have reached 700+ receiving yards since 2021, and Sadiq is cheap enough (150, TE17) to see if the trend continues. *(Added May 28)*

##### __Miami Dolphins__

+   __De’Von Achane__ underwent a clean-up procedure on his shoulder this off-season, which has him watching from the sidelines during OTA practices. He said he hopes to return to full action by the start of training camp. The Dolphins weren’t too concerned about his shoulder surgery when they made him one of the highest-paid RBs, inking him to a four-year, $64 million contract in mid-May, which included $32 million guaranteed. Miami will take its time with Achane this summer since he’s set to handle a massive workload once again after totaling 305 touches and 1838 scrimmage yards in 16 games in his third season. He’s being selected in the second round (14, RB7) because his upside could be capped by the addition of a mobile quarterback in __Malik Willis__ and Miami’s lack of offensive weapons around Achane. *(Added May 28)*

##### __Philadelphia Eagles/New England Patriots__

+   Ian Rapoport [reported](https://x.com/RapSheet/status/2059778095243018501?s=20) that the Patriots and Eagles are “not particularly close” on the required compensation to complete a trade for __A.J. Brown__, whose cap hit drops from $43 million to $16.4 million if he’s traded after June 1. The Eagles are seeking a first-round pick for Brown, who has reached 1000+ receiving yards in six of his first seven seasons. Brown hasn’t attended Eagles’ OTA workouts this spring, and __Jalen Hurts__ spoke about his playing time with Brown in the past tense when asked about the disgruntled WR. Brown is still likely to be moved to New England this summer, but a potential trade may have to wait until closer to training camp, which opens up the potential for other suitors to enter the mix. *(Added May 28)*

##### __Arizona Cardinals__

+   __Jacoby Brissett__ wasn’t present for the start of Arizona’s voluntary OTAs as he seeks a pay raise on his $4.88 million contract, with just $1.5 million guaranteed for the 2026 season. He’s still being paid like a backup despite the organization [informing him](https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/48810874/without-jacoby-brissett-mike-lafleur-cardinals-open-otas) that he would open the season as the starter. ESPN’s Josh Weinfuss reported that the two sides remained “significantly” apart as of May 22. Arizona handed __Gardner Minshew__ $5.14 million in guaranteed money in free agency before selecting __Carson Beck__ at No. 65, so Brissett is unlikely to get a hefty raise before the season. Brissett is missing out on reps in a new offense, but __Mike LaFleur__ said he wasn’t concerned about the 10-year veteran falling behind. He ranked as the QB7 (19.9 FPG) from Week 6 through the end of the season, but he won’t drop back 45.8 times per game as he did last season. Brissett isn’t the easiest click in best ball drafts, even at this suppressed ADP (190, QB30). The Cards are likely to be out of postseason contention, and they’ll want to take a look at Beck during the best ball money-making weeks. Brissett is much more intriguing in 2-QB/Superflex redraft leagues if you want to punt your second-QB spot until the middle rounds of the draft and use Brissett until he eventually is benched later in the season. *(Updated May 28)*

##### __Indianapolis Colts__

+   __Patrick Mahomes__ grabbed the quarterback headlines for his appearance at Chiefs OTAs, but __Daniel Jones__ participated in individual drills at OTAs on May 26 as he’s nearly six months removed from right Achilles surgery. ESPN’s Stephen Holder [wrote](https://x.com/HolderStephen/status/2059453466271993871?s=20) that Jones appears likely to avoid the PUP list to start training camp at this point, and Jones [told reporters](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7313723/2026/05/28/colts-daniel-jones-week-1-start-anthony-richardson-sr-trade-request/) that he’ll “absolutely” be ready for Week 1 against the Ravens. Jones leveled up in his first season under __Shane Steichen__, showing more confidence and better timing on his way to posting career-highs in completion percentage (68%), YPA (8.1), passing YPG (238.5), and QB rating (100.2). He’s coming off his best TD rate (4.9%) since his rookie season and his second-most rushing TDs (5) in his seven-year career on his way to finishing as the QB13 (18.2 FPG). He’s going to take a step back, but it appears he’ll be ready for the season opener, and he’s a value at his current QB3 ADP (145, QB25). *(Updated May 28)*

May 27
------

##### __Denver Broncos__

+   *The Athletic*’s Nick Kosmider [wrote](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7309414/2026/05/27/denver-broncos-davis-webb/) that Denver’s offense could play with more tempo this season with __Davis Webb__ taking over as the playcaller for __Sean Payton__, who will still have a major say in the identity of the offense. Payton said his “dissemination” of the play calls has slowed in recent years, and he expects Webb will get plays out more quickly and efficiently. The Broncos ranked seventh in plays per game (64.1) and 12th in seconds per play (29.2) under Payton last season. I’m not banking on Webb speeding up Denver’s offense in a substantial enough way to change my outlook on Broncos skill players, but I’ll use it as a small tiebreaker just in case Denver’s offense does have slightly more volume this season. *(Added May 27)*

##### __Kansas City Chiefs__

+   __Patrick Mahomes__ participated in Chiefs OTAs on May 27, which was yet another sign that Mahomes is on track for the start of the season — he’s more than five months removed from ACL and LCL surgery in mid-December. The NFL gave it away that he’ll be ready for Week 1 when they scheduled the Chiefs to host the Broncos on Monday Night Football. I figured the schedule-makers would backload Kansas City’s primetime games and division contests just in case Mahomes was unable to play in the first month of the season. Instead, the Chiefs have one of their most important games on Monday Night Football in the season opener at Arrowhead Stadium. Mahomes should see his ADP (93, QB12) tick up throughout the summer if it continues to look like he’ll be ready for Week 1, and I’ll be passing on him at his rising price. __Rashee Rice__ is tough to trust to be available for a full season, and Mahomes’ career-best 5.2 FP as a runner will be unsustainable coming off a major knee injury. *(Added May 27)*

##### __Seattle Seahawks__

+   __Tory Horton__ could return to team workouts by the end of spring workouts, [according to](https://x.com/johnpboyle/status/2059388699369197932?s=20) __Mike Macdonald__. Horton suffered a season-ending shin injury in Week 9, and Macdonald said that Horton received some good news in late May that could accelerate his return. Horton looked the part as a fifth-round pick before his injury, scoring 5 receiving TDs on just 22 targets and a punt-return TD in eight games. He’ll battle __Rashid Shaheed__ and __Cooper Kupp__ for the limited WR available behind __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__. Horton is off the fantasy radar to open the season and a player to stash on dynasty benches. *(Added May 27)*

May 26
------

##### __Tampa Bay Buccaneers__

+   GM __Jason Licht__ [said](https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bucs/2026/05/16/bucky-irving-kenneth-gainwell-sean-tucker-rachaad-white-zac-robinson/) __Bucky Irving__ would be limited during OTAs but should be ready for training camp. He suffered a left shoulder injury in Week 4 last season and missed seven straight games due to the issue and an ankle injury. He never regained his form even when he returned to the lineup, and he needed [offseason surgery](https://www.joebucsfan.com/2026/02/bucky-irving-had-offseason-shoulder-surgery/) to repair the lingering shoulder issue. Irving mentally struggled to get over his first major injury, and it shouldn’t be a huge surprise that the Buccaneers are taking it slow with Irving at this time of year. HC __Todd Bowles__ was more pessimistic about Bucky’s timeline than Licht, telling the media that he expected Bucky back in the summer *or fall*. The Buccaneers paid __Kenneth Gainwell__ $9.83 million guaranteed to be a high-end #2 option behind Tampa Bay’s 2024 fourth-round pick. Gainwell has a history of earning a bigger role than expected, and this backfield is setting up to be a potential three-man committee. Bucky was already a tough click at his ADP (45, RB19) since he could be a between-the-20s player, with Gainwell stealing passing-game snaps and __Sean Tucker__ vulturing goal-line opportunities. He’ll be an even tougher click with his availability for the start of the season a bit up in the air, even with his ADP expected to slide. *(Updated May 26)*

##### __Kansas City Chiefs__

+   __Rashee Rice__ is once again in trouble with the law. He triggered a 30-day jail sentence by testing positive for THC, which violated his five-year deferred probation for a third-degree felony charge last summer. He’ll miss Chiefs OTAs and mandatory minicamp while he serves jail time until June 16. He faced a six-game suspension to start last season for driving nearly 120 mph and causing a multi-car crash on a Dallas highway in March 2024. The NFL announced in early April that it closed its investigation into abuse allegations and that he wouldn’t face any additional discipline from the league. Rice’s career is on thin ice after his latest misstep, even if he doesn’t face an additional suspension for his latest legal issue. He could face a much longer jail sentence or have his probation revoked completely if he can’t stay out of his own way for the 4+ years remaining on his probation. It’s also the reason the Chiefs have no plans to give Rice an extension before the start of the season ([per Adam Schefter](https://x.com/AdamSchefter/status/2057133904243356064?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2057133904243356064%7Ctwgr%5E2096cc2bc300069ea19f01757af13599222b01f5%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fchiefswire.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fnfl%2Fchiefs%2F2026%2F05%2F26%2Fnfl-insider-believes-kansas-city-chiefs-wr-rashee-rice-is-hurting-his-contract-extension-hopes%2F90252371007%2F)). It also came out that Rice needed to have a clean-up procedure on his right knee a week before he was ordered to serve jail time. Rice’s dynasty value takes another significant hit with the latest news, and he’s a riskier pick for the upcoming season, especially if the Chiefs decide to protect themselves by signing a player like __Stefon Diggs__ in the coming weeks. *(Updated May 26)*

##### __Cleveland Browns__

+   *The Athletic*’s Zac Jackson [noted](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7300401/2026/05/26/browns-rookie-report-spencer-fano-denzel-boston/) __KC Concepcion__ is fast in early workouts. He also added that Concepcion has been moved around the formation and used in heavy motion in early installs as they try to “hunt favorable matchups” for their first-round WR. __Zay Flowers__ flourished under __Todd Monken__ in Baltimore, and Monken will use Concepcion like Flowers. Monken will put him in motion and use him to stretch the field, and he’ll also get Concepcion the ball in space to take advantage of his ability with the ball in his hands. The biggest concern for Concepcion is the quarterback play he’ll receive from __Deshaun Watson__ and __Shedeur Sanders__, but he’s worth betting on at [+3000 odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-rookie-of-the-year-awards#/) to win the Offensive Rookie of the Year. *(Added May 26)*

May 24
------

##### __San Francisco 49ers__

+   ESPN’s Nick Wagoner [wrote](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48829524/san-francisco-2026-nfl-49ers-depth-chart-running-back-christian-mccaffrey-kaelon-black) that 2025 fifth-round pick __Jordan James__ is the most likely to win the backup spot behind __Christian McCaffrey__. He’ll be in a training camp battle with third-round pick __Kaelon Black__ and __Isaac Guerendo__ for the valuable handcuff role in __Kyle Shanahan__’s prolific rushing offense. Shanahan said of James, “\[He\] came on really strong at the end of last year, but he missed so much in the beginning. He kind of just missed his window to pass some other people up. I wish I would have got him on the field more than I did…He needs to take that next step.” James is a free pick in the final round of best ball drafts (215, RB67), but he could have one of the more valuable handcuff spots behind the oft-injured CMC if he can win the #2 spot in training camp. *(Added May 24)*

##### __Los Angeles Rams__

+   __Matthew Stafford__ and the Rams agreed to a one-year, $55 million extension through the 2027 season, and it’s worth up to $60 million in incentives. Stafford is on a year-to-year basis with his playing career as he enters his age-38, and __Sean McVay__ revealed that Stafford nearly started last season on the IR because of his back issue. The Rams clearly know Stafford could be done at any point after stunning the league by drafting __Ty Simpson__ 13th overall. Stafford could’ve used another weapon in a thin receiving corps behind __Puka Nacua__ and __Davante Adams__, and his star receivers have off-the-field and injury concerns, respectively. Stafford is set to regress off his MVP season based on his early ADP (104, QB15), and he has some downside if Puka or Davante miss extended time. *(Updated May 24)*

##### __New York Giants__

+   __John Harbaugh__ [told the media](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48837807/harbaugh-nabers-knee-injury-not-simple-clouding-return-date) that __Malik Nabers__ is recovering from “not a simple knee” injury, and he said he’s not sure when Nabers will return to the field. He tore his right ACL in late September, which required surgery and a full meniscus repair in October. He also underwent a second procedure this offseason to remove scar tissue in his knee. It’s looking more and more likely that Nabers won’t be ready for the start of the season, and his ADP (23, WR8) will continue to fall into the third round. He still has late-season appeal when the money is awarded in leagues, but he could be slow out of the gates for the first month or two of the season. *(Added May 24)*

##### __Philadelphia Eagles__

+   __Jalen Hurts__ is set to have a new playcaller for the 11th straight season since he enrolled at Alabama for the 2016 season. __Sean Mannion__ is taking over for __Kevin Patullo__ for the 2026 season, and he comes from a __Sean McVay__\-__Matt LaFleur__ background. *The Athletic*’s Zach Berman wrote that Mannion’s new scheme will include more under-center plays, including play-action from under center. Hurts is coming off a career-low 26.3 rushing YPG since he became the full-time starter in 2021. Mannion said Hurts’ legs will be a part of his wide-zone running scheme, but it won’t be the only part of it. Hurts is likely to lose __A.J. Brown__ in the near future, but there’s optimism Hurts can get back on track at a cheaper ADP (69, QB5) under his new playcaller. *(Added May 24)*

##### __Tennessee Titans__

+   __Cam Ward__ said he’s shed 10 pounds this offseason since playing at a listed 219 pounds as a rookie. He thinks playing at a lighter weight will help with his durability and his speed in the pocket. He also said he worked on strengthening his right shoulder after spraining it in the season finale, and is having no issues with it this spring. Ward needs to run a little more in __Brian Daboll__’s offense to boost his fantasy value heading into his second season. He posted only 39/159/2 rushing as a rookie, including just 14 scrambles for 108 yards. *(Added May 24)*

##### __Free Agent__

+   Former Dolphins WR __Tyreek Hill__ may not be ready to play until the middle of the season, [per Adam Schefter](https://www.nbcsports.com/fantasy/football/player-news?p=2). The free agent WR suffered multiple ligament tears and a knee dislocation in the fourth game of last season. Hill has relied heavily on speed and quickness, and it’s fair to wonder if he’ll have the same twitchiness entering his age-32 season, if he’s able to play at all in 2026. It also doesn’t help that he brings plenty of off-the-field baggage with him to his next location. Hill may have to wait until the start of the season to land a short-term, incentive-laden contract once he’s able to prove he’s healthy and close to playing football again. *(Added May 24)*

May 22
------

##### __Las Vegas Raiders__

+   __Ashton Jeanty__ is being drafted like he’ll be a bell-cow back with a first-round ADP (12, RB6), but __Klint Kubiak__ notably rotated __Kenneth Walker__ and __Zach Charbonnet__ in Seattle last season. The Raiders also selected __Mike Washington__ in the fourth round, but Kubiak is ready to get plenty of mileage out of Jeanty this season. Kubiak said, “It’s important to have a quality second back, but the best player has got to play, and we’ve got to get them on the field as much as we can…Christian McCaffrey, his play-snap percentage is high. So, those great backs, they don’t want to come off the field.” Jeanty also spoke about staying on the field as much as possible after he finished fourth in snap share (77.9%), second in carry share (72.1%), and seventh in route share (52.2%) as a rookie. Jeanty’s path to a massive role is intact unless Washington forces Kubiak to get him involved with a strong training camp. Jeanty needs a better offensive environment and better blocking — he finished second to last in YBC/ATT (1.28) — to pay off his current ADP. *(Added May 22)*

May 21
------

##### __Los Angeles Chargers__

+   GM __Joe Hortiz__ [told Kay Adams](https://x.com/UpAndAdamsShow/status/2057491131907113435?s=20) that the team hasn’t “closed the door” on __Keenan Allen__ returning to the franchise for a 13th season. He also said, “We’re letting these young guys get a chance…Our guys that we have here, we’re letting them grow and develop.” The next month of practices will decide whether the Chargers go into training camp with __Ladd McConkey__, __Quentin Johnston__, __Tre’ Harris__, __KeAndre Lambert-Smith__, and __Brenen Thompson__ at the top of the WR depth chart, or if the team will sign Allen and slot him back in as the #3 WR. The Chargers let their young WRs get more reps in OTAs and minicamp last summer before signing Allen in the first week of August. Allen’s presence would be a major drag on the fantasy values of McConkey and company after he led the Chargers in TPRR (.26) at 33 years old. The additions of __Alec Ingold__, __Charlie Kolar__, and __David Njoku__ indicate that the Chargers are moving toward a heavier personnel approach under __Mike McDaniel__. There’s a decent chance Hortiz was just being respectful of a Chargers legend, which could create a small buying opportunity if McConkey’s fourth-round ADP (41, WR20) slips a bit. *(Added May 21)*

##### __Buffalo Bills__

+   __Dalton Kincaid__ has flashed elite TE traits early in his career, but he’s been a part-time player in Buffalo’s offense and has been unable to stay healthy. Better health could go a long way to increasing Kincaid’s opportunities in 2026, which would help him realize his full fantasy potential. He owns just a 57% route share in 42 of a possible 51 career games since the Bills selected him in the first round in 2023. Kincaid opted against surgery to fix a PCL injury he’s dealt with since 2014, electing to rehab the injury based on the recommendations of the doctors he talked to about his condition. He [said it’s the best he’s felt so far in his career](https://x.com/NickSabatoGNN/status/2056839766138569038?s=20), which was helped by adding 10-12 pounds of muscle this offseason. Kincaid led the league in TPRR (.27) and YPRR (3.19) among 53 TEs who ran 150+ routes, but he ranked seventh in route share (44.2%) among Bills receivers — he even ranked behind __Dawson Knox__ at 48.2%. I’ve been hoping that Kincaid could stay healthy and run more routes since he broke into the league, but it hasn’t happened yet heading into his fourth season. The Bills notably picked up his fifth-year option this spring, which is a sign that they could have bigger plans for him. It seems unlikely that __Joe Brady__ changes his approach at TE as he moves from offensive coordinator to head coach. It’s still worth taking a shot on Kincaid at his depressed ADP (131, TE13) because he has top-five potential at the position if he could ever get close to a 70% route share. *(Updated May 21)*

##### __Las Vegas Raiders__

+   ESPN’s Ryan McFadden believes the expectation is for __Kirk Cousins__ to open the season as the starting quarterback over first overall pick __Fernando Mendoza__. It’s not a big surprise, but Cousins received all of the first-team reps at early OTAs, while Mendoza worked mostly with rookies behind __Aidan O’Connell__. Mendoza will be watching from the sidelines in September if minority owner __Tom Brady__ has as much influence as it seems from the outside. Brady previously called it a “[tragedy](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/zyclRMckosM?sttick=0)” to force rookie quarterbacks to play early in their careers. The Raiders will pay $11.3 million guaranteed to Cousins to mentor Mendoza this season, which is a starter’s salary and makes him the 20th-highest-paid QB in average annual value. The bigger question is when Mendoza will enter the starting lineup. The Raiders don’t have any obvious on-ramps to get Mendoza in the lineup because all of their games are on Sunday, and their bye week doesn’t arrive until Week 13. Mendoza is off the radar in redraft leagues and a player to stash in 2-QB/Superflex formats to open the season. Cousins is a QB3 option for at least September in 2-QB/Superflex leagues. *(Added May 21)*

May 20
------

##### __Buffalo Bills__

+   __Josh Allen__ is participating in Buffalo’s offseason program as he promised after undergoing surgery in late January to remove a bone chip from his right foot. A healthy Allen is getting some initial work in with his new receiver, __DJ Moore__, who is coming off the worst season of his career before getting traded to the Bills. Allen is the clear QB1 this draft season with an ADP of 30, and he’s going a full two rounds earlier than the QB2, __Lamar Jackson__. *(Added May 20)*

##### __New England Patriots__

+   __Kayshon Boutte__ has been working out [away from the team](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48780703/new-england-patriots-notebook-longest-tenured-employee-nancy-meier-retire) facility during New England’s voluntary offseason program, which is a sign he could still be on the trade block after the Patriots were reportedly shopping him before and during the draft. It’s worth selecting Boutte in the final rounds of your best ball drafts if you picked __Jalen Hurts__ in the sixth or seventh round, since there’s a good chance Boutte and a future first-round pick could be coming to Philadelphia in exchange for Brown. *(Added May 20)*

##### __Cleveland Browns__

+   __Quinshon Judkins__ participated in voluntary minicamp in late April and in voluntary OTA workouts on May 20, which is five months after he suffered a dislocated ankle and a fractured fibula, which required surgery on Dec. 23. His initial recovery timeline called for 4-6 months off before returning to football activity, so it appears he’s on track to be ready for training camp. Judkins and __Cam Skattebo__ are both returning from fractured fibulas. Ryan Heath [laid out](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2056752913913991666) how players returning from similar injuries have been fantasy potholes in the recent past. Judkins is looking to break that trend behind a revamped offensive line in __Todd Monken__’s new offense. He should rack up plenty of carries to justify selecting him as an RB2 at his fifth-round ADP (55, RB23), but it’s tough to build a massive upside case since he could lose passing-game snaps to __Dylan Sampson__ in what is shaping up to be a spread offense. *(Added May 20)*

##### __San Francisco 49ers__

+   *The Athletic*’s Matt Barrows broke down San Francisco’s receiving corps in a [recent mailbag](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7289584/2026/05/19/49ers-schedule-wide-receivers/). He believes __Mike Evans__ will play the X, __Ricky Pearsall__ will line up at Z, and __Christian Kirk__ and second-round pick __De’Zhaun Stribling__ will compete to be the slot receiver. He also thinks Stribling will train to be the backup X receiver behind Evans, and Kirk will be the backup Z receiver behind Pearsall. Those backup distinctions could be important when we’re working the waiver wire later this year because of Evans’ and Pearsall’s durability issues. Evans missed 10 games in the last two seasons, and Pearsall sat out 14 contests in his first two seasons. *(Added May 20)*

##### __Pittsburgh Steelers__

+   The Steelers and __Aaron Rodgers__ finally came to terms on a one-year, $22 million guaranteed deal that is worth up to $25 million. He said on May 20 that this upcoming season would be his last, but he admitted he thought 2025 would be his final season after __Mike Tomlin__ stepped away before being drawn back in by the Steelers' hiring __Mike McCarthy__. Rodgers wanted the ball out of his hands last season, finishing with the fastest average time to throw (2.38 seconds) and the fourth-lowest aDOT (6.3 yards) among 45 QBs who attempted 100+ passes. The style of play led him to rank 10th in catchable throw rate (76.9%) and fourth in turnover-worthy throw rate (1.6%), but 31st in hero throw rate (3.8%). He’s posted a solid 4.8% TD rate in each of his last three healthy campaigns, but he’s unlikely to do much better at 42 years old. The Steelers at least added __Michael Pittman__ and __Germie Bernard__ to a receiving corps that ranked 31st in 11 personnel (38.9%) under playcaller __Arthur Smith__. Rodgers will step into a familiar offense under his longtime Packers HC, whose offense ranked ninth in 11 personnel (70.8%) in his final season with the Cowboys. Rodgers won two of his four MVPs under McCarthy, but those days are long gone. He should at least have a little more upside than his QB27 (14.7) from last season, with a better receiving corps around him. *(Updated May 20)*

May 19
------

##### __Cleveland Browns__

+   The Browns are laying the early groundwork to name __Deshaun Watson__ as the Week 1 starter over __Shedeur Sanders__ once training camp rolls around. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler [heard](https://x.com/ESPNCleveland/status/2056121255984566332?s=20) Watson has “hit it off with __Todd Monken__”, and Mary Kay Cabot [reported](https://x.com/MaryKayCabot/status/2049523640450871504?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet) in late April that Watson took the lead over Sanders. The decision to go with Watson is also another indication that Monken’s offense could be more of a spread attack than his TE-heavy attack in Baltimore. The Browns already selected __KC Concepcion__ and __Denzel Boston__ inside the top 39 picks to bolster their WR depth, and Watson previously struggled in __Kevin Stefanski__’s under-center offense. Watson is entering the final year of his disastrous five-year, $230 million contract he signed in 2022, and the Browns clearly want to take one final look at Watson since they’re paying him so much money. The Browns can also ice the Shedeur hype early in the season, but he’ll eventually get opportunities to play later in the season once Watson flames out. *(Added May 19)*
